themes.label: Sound
themes.headline: Build your own focus atmosphere.
themes.summary: Music, nature sounds or silence: the right atmosphere is a choice.
themes.design: Optional audio, volume control and no automatic playback.
themes.question: Which sound, if any, helps this person with this task?
themes.limit: Preference is not measured performance. White-noise findings in specific populations cannot establish a benefit for everyone, and nature recordings are not laboratory white noise.

themes.label: Accountability
themes.headline: A quiet sense of studying alongside someone.
themes.summary: Shared presence can be a prompt to begin; it should remain optional.
themes.design: Friend presence and focus-time summaries without requiring a video call.
themes.question: Does visibility help people start and return, or add comparison pressure?
themes.limit: Goal monitoring, live co-study and social presence are different mechanisms. None proves that elapsed time was spent learning.

themes.label: Motivation
themes.headline: Turn time into something personal.
themes.summary: Discoveries become a wardrobe and a home worth returning to.
themes.design: Cosmetic choice, visible progress and the freedom to pause.
themes.question: Are people moving their chosen task forward, or collecting with an idle timer?
themes.limit: Rewards do not universally outperform punishment. Pomodoro itself is a time-structuring technique. Current Eumo sessions retain earned rewards when ended early.

themes.label: Companionship
themes.headline: A companion that works and rests with you.
themes.summary: The mole is always part of the experience. AI conversation is optional.
themes.design: A persistent character plus optional planning and conversation support.
themes.question: Does companionship make starting easier and remain helpful after the novelty fades?
themes.limit: Loneliness, demand for AI, sustained benefit and willingness to pay are separate questions. Eumo does not claim to replace human relationships or provide treatment.

sources.citation: Kämpfe, J., Sedlmeier, P., & Renkewitz, F. (2011). The impact of background music on adult listeners: A meta-analysis. Psychology of Music.
sources.scope: Background music in adult listeners; task and outcome differences must be checked.

sources.citation: Lesiuk, T. (2005). The effect of music on work performance. Psychology of Music.
sources.scope: Work context; population, design and limits require verification before generalization.

sources.citation: Harkin, B., et al. (2016). Does monitoring goal progress promote goal attainment? A meta-analysis of the experimental evidence. Psychological Bulletin.
sources.scope: Goal progress monitoring; not direct evidence for Eumo, Discord co-study or body doubling.

sources.citation: Deci, E. L., Koestner, R., & Ryan, R. M. (1999). A meta-analytic review of experiments examining the effects of extrinsic rewards on intrinsic motivation. Psychological Bulletin.
sources.scope: Extrinsic rewards and intrinsic motivation; reward type and contingency need careful interpretation.

sources.citation: Cerasoli, C. P., Nicklin, J. M., & Ford, M. T. (2014). Intrinsic motivation and extrinsic incentives jointly predict performance: A 40-year meta-analysis. Psychological Bulletin.
sources.scope: Intrinsic motivation, incentives and performance; not a blanket endorsement of game rewards.

sources.citation: Ta, V., et al. (2020). User Experiences of Social Support From Companion Chatbots in Everyday Contexts: Thematic Analysis. Journal of Medical Internet Research.
sources.scope: Qualitative reported experiences; not population prevalence, causal efficacy or purchase demand.

sources.citation: AI Companions Reduce Loneliness (2024 research lead; bibliographic details and current version pending verification).
sources.scope: Check participants, duration, comparators and outcomes; do not extrapolate to learning or long-term well-being.

market.beachhead: Young-adult students and early-career desk workers who prefer a gentle focus ritual.
market.status: Proposed initial segment; market size and willingness to pay remain unvalidated.
market.children: A separate future discovery workstream, not the initial target.
market.business: Subscriptions, cosmetic skins and physical extensions are revenue hypotheses.

validation: Observe first-session and decorating tasks; record actual participants and methods.
Measure time to start and task success, with no invented baseline or improvement percentage.
Follow repeat use, chosen-task progress, collecting distraction and comparison pressure.
Test sound and friend visibility as optional conditions.
Evaluate willingness to pay after use; distinguish stated interest from purchases.
